ml_interpretation.problem_statement: Binary classification: predict whether a lead reaches Closed Won (is_won=1) from lead source, source group, notes sentiment, and notes word count.
ml_interpretation.key_finding: Both models achieve ROC-AUC ~0.505 — marginally above random chance (0.5). This is the honest, expected result given the dataset structure: all 20 sources have nearly identical win rates (9.28%-10.69%), and notes sentiment shows no meaningful correlation with outcome. The dataset does not contain enough discriminative signal in the available features to build a practically useful predictive model.
why_limited_predictability: Source win rates span only 1.4 percentage points across 20 channels — insufficient differentiation
Notes sentiment mean is nearly identical across Won (0.0575), Lost (0.0646), and Open (0.0621) outcomes
Notes word count shows no meaningful difference by outcome
Lead Owner and Company fields were correctly excluded as quasi-identifiers (~93k unique owners for 100k records)
No temporal, financial, or behavioral features exist in the dataset
what_the_model_does_capture: Notes sentiment and word count account for 90% of Random Forest feature importance — but this reflects their numeric variance, not genuine predictive power
Source-level features (Podcast, Partner Program, Networking Event) appear in the top 10 by importance, consistent with the small but real win-rate spread observed in EDA
ml_interpretation.correct_interpretation: The ~1.4 percentage point spread in win rates across sources IS a real analytical finding useful for business prioritisation (e.g. invest more in Podcast/Referral channels). However, this signal is too weak for a lead-level binary classifier to be practically actionable. A ROC-AUC of 0.509 means the model is essentially guessing.
ml_interpretation.causal_warning: Correlation between source and win rate does NOT imply that the source causes the win. Other unmeasured factors (lead quality, industry, deal size) likely drive outcomes.
ml_interpretation.recommendation: Use the source-level win rate analytics (from EDA/SQL phases) for channel investment decisions. For a practically useful ML model, additional features would be needed: deal size, industry, engagement score, response time, number of follow-ups, etc.
